home.title: Not Yet: ADHD Routine App, Alarm Clock & App Blocker
home.og_title: Not Yet · Start. Keep going. Stop when it’s time.
home.description: Built with ADHD in mind: routines that change before they get boring, an alarm clock one tap won’t stop, and app locks for focus and bedtime.
home.hero_more: See a day with Not Yet
home.fan_label: A day with the app, from the alarm to bedtime
home.alt_hero_alarm: The alarm ringing at 6:15, with the “Wake-up task” button.
home.alt_hero_home: Not Yet, an ADHD-friendly routine app. Home at 7:05: the morning routine is ready, Run #24.
home.pillars_title: Routines, alarms, a weekly planner and app locks in one app.
home.start_alarm_text: Rings even on silent. Only stops after three quick tasks, a shake, a few steps or an NFC tag.
home.start_noapp_text: The routine shows up on your Lock Screen at its time. Start it right there.
home.stay_rotation_text: Wheel, tickets, dice, boss fight. It changes before it gets old.
home.stay_focus_text: Allow only a few apps, or block the ones that pull you away, until the time is up.
home.stay_coins_text: Steps earn coins. Spend them on a coffee or an episode.
home.stop_title: An actual end to the day.
home.stop_adult_text: Blocks adult websites around the clock, and any other sites you add. Lock it for a while, and switching it off takes 24 hours.
home.day1_title: One tap won’t stop this alarm.
home.day1_text: Tap “Wake-up task” and do one: three quick tasks, a shake, a few steps or an NFC tag. Then it goes quiet.
home.alt_alarm: The alarm ringing, with the “Wake-up task” button.
home.day2_title: Morning routine from the Lock Screen.
home.day2_text: Six steps, about 30 minutes. Today the wheel picks the order.
home.day3_text: Only the apps you allowed will open. Everything else waits until the time is up.
home.day4_text: Say how much time you have. Get one to-do that fits.
home.alt_sidequest: Sidequest: pick how much time you have.
home.day5_text: Run #24 is done. Four hits to go. About 35 coins inside.
home.alt_runend: Run end: Run #24, some of it, a piggy bank to smash.
home.day6_text: Home says nothing needs doing, and water nudges stop. At 23:00 the lock follows.
home.rot_lead: The way a routine plays changes every few runs, before it gets old. Never back to one of the last two.
home.gesture_tally: Tap the card to click the counter.
home.gesture_rocket: Hold the card until the rocket lifts off.
home.alt_rot_wheel: Wheel: tap or flick to spin.
home.alt_rot_tally: Tally counter: tap the card to click the counter.
home.alt_rot_rocket: Rocket: hold the card until it lifts off.
home.rot_more: Also in the rotation: dice, boss fight, cards, blind run.
home.stance_title: No streaks. No guilt. No red numbers.
home.stance1_yes: Run #24. Some of it. That counts.
home.stance2_yes: Stopped for now. It stays on the list.
home.stance5_yes: Welcome back. A short one today.
home.week_text: Tap the date on Home to see the next seven days. Drop a to-do into a free spot: roughly then, no deadline. When it’s time, the reminder shows the to-do’s icon.
home.alt_week: Week, Tuesday: a birthday, the morning routine, an alarm, lunch from the calendar and two planned to-dos.
home.feat_watch_text: Start a run, check off steps and log water from your wrist.
home.alt_watch: Apple Watch run: Skincare, step 3 of 6, checked off with a stamp.
home.alt_watch_start: Apple Watch: Morning, Run #24, about 21 minutes. One tap starts it.
home.feat_widgets_text: The current step on your Lock Screen. Check it off right there.
home.alt_widget_s: Small widget with the next routine.
home.alt_widget_m: Medium widget with the current run.
home.alt_live: Lock Screen: the Morning routine, Run #24, ready to start.
home.feat_water_text: One tap per glass, from Home, widget or watch. Nudges only while you’re up.
home.feat_todos_text: Got 30 minutes? Get one to-do that fits.
home.alt_sidequest_crop: Sidequest: how much time do you have?
home.feat_nfc_text: Tap the tag on your bathroom mirror. The routine that belongs there starts.
home.faq_friendly_a: Yes. It’s built for ADHD: short steps, a routine that changes before it gets boring, and no streaks to lose. It’s also for anyone who finds starting or stopping hard. No diagnosis needed.
home.faq_devices_q: Which devices does it run on?
home.faq_devices_a: iPhone with iOS 26 or later, from the App Store. There’s also an app for Apple Watch: start a routine, check off steps and log water from your wrist.
home.faq_android_a: It’s in development, as an app of its own.
home.faq_lang_q: Which languages does the app speak?
home.faq_lang_a: English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Japanese and Korean. It follows your iPhone’s language, and you can pick another one just for Not Yet in the iOS Settings app.
home.faq_a11y_q: Does it work with large text and reduced motion?
home.faq_a11y_a: Yes. Not Yet follows your iPhone’s text size, including the largest accessibility sizes, and tones down its animations when you’ve asked for less motion.
home.faq_alarm_q: Will the alarm clock really get me up?
home.faq_alarm_a: It rings even on silent, and there’s no snooze. It only stops once you’ve finished three quick tasks, shaken your phone, walked a few steps or scanned an NFC tag.
home.faq_morning_q: Does it help with my morning routine?
home.faq_morning_a: Yes. Set it up once, step by step. It shows up on your Lock Screen at its time, and you check off steps right there. If you use the alarm, the routine can start right after the wake-up task.
home.faq_locks_q: How do the app locks work?
home.faq_locks_a: Focus lock works as an app blocker: it allows only a few apps, or blocks the ones that pull you away, until the time is up. Bedtime lock does the same at night, until it’s time to get up. Not Yet never sees which apps you pick.
home.faq_night_q: Can it lock my phone at night?
home.faq_night_a: It locks the apps you pick, not the whole phone. Plan your nights like alarms: one for weekdays, one for the weekend. First you wind down, then Bedtime lock keeps those apps locked until it’s time to get up.
home.faq_calendar_q: Does it work with my calendar?
home.faq_calendar_a: Yes. Birthdays become a step, events show up in Week, and planned to-dos can appear in your calendar app, in a calendar of their own.
home.faq_data_a: On your iPhone and Apple Watch, in your iPhone backups and, if you turn it on, in Not Yet’s own backup in your iCloud. No account, no tracking in the app, and nothing is sent to us. Details in the privacy policy.
home.faq_more: Something else, or something not working? Write to info@not-yet.app or see Support. A real person reads every message.
home.alt_cta: Run end: Run #24. Some of it. That counts.
home.og_sub: Built with ADHD in mind. iPhone and Apple Watch.
home.hero_sub: An alarm that gets you out of bed, routines that never stay the same for long, and locks for focus and bedtime.
home.alt_hero_boss: Morning run with a boss fight: the longest step comes last.
home.alt_hero_week: Week: the next seven days, with a free spot for a to-do.
home.alt_hero_nights: Nights: bedtime plans for office days, work-from-home days and the weekend.
home.pillars_lead: Made for the moments that usually go wrong.
home.stop_nights_text: Plan your nights like alarms: one for weekdays, one for the weekend. First you wind down, then the apps you picked stay locked until it’s time to get up.
home.alt_lock: Lock Screen with the morning run: check off the current step right there.
home.alt_focus: Home in the morning: Focus lock is on, 42 minutes left.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: Privacy policy for the Not Yet app and not-yet.app. No account, no tracking in the app. Your data stays on your devices and, if you want, in your own iCloud.
privacy.short_dd: No sign-up, and no server of ours that stores your data.
privacy.short_dd2: Routines, runs, to-dos, coins and settings live on your iPhone, its widgets and your Apple Watch.
privacy.short_dd3: Not Yet’s iCloud backup is off until you turn it on. It goes to your own private iCloud, where we can’t read it. iPhone backups to iCloud include the app’s data too.
privacy.short_dd_calendar: With “Add to Calendar” on, Not Yet adds planned to-dos to its own calendar, called “Not Yet”. Nothing is shared or analysed.
privacy.short_dd4: No analytics, ads or tracking in the app. No cookies on this website.
privacy.short_dd5: GitHub hosts this website and keeps server logs with IP addresses. We don’t see them.
privacy.short_dd_purchases: Apple handles Not Yet Plus. We get no payment data, no name and no Apple ID.

GitHub stores this in server logs. We have no access to these logs and receive no visitor statistics from GitHub. GitHub may process this data in the USA. GitHub, Inc. is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework. Details: GitHub General Privacy Statement.

privacy.website_p4: This website sets no cookies and loads nothing from other companies: fonts, images, styles and scripts come from not-yet.app itself, the visit counter from our own subdomain a.not-yet.app (see below). There are no forms, embedded videos, maps or social media buttons. If you switch to dark mode or pick a language, your browser remembers that choice in its local storage on your device; it is never sent anywhere.
privacy.email_p: If you email us, for example at info@not-yet.app, we use your email address, your name if you give it and your message only to answer you. Emails to this address are stored in our mailbox at Infomaniak Network SA in Geneva, Switzerland. The EU Commission has issued an adequacy decision for Switzerland.
privacy.email_p2: You can join the beta directly through our public TestFlight link. That happens between you and Apple, and Apple’s TestFlight terms and privacy policy apply. In App Store Connect we see only the tester details Apple shows us; for people who join through the public link, that usually doesn’t include an email address. If you write to us instead, for example because the beta is full, we use your email address only to answer you and to invite you. For an invite by email, we enter your address, and your name if you gave it, in App Store Connect, and Apple sends you the TestFlight invite.
privacy.email_p3: Legal basis is your request (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) and our legitimate interest in answering messages (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). We delete emails when they are no longer needed, and at any time on request. You can leave the beta at any time in the TestFlight app; on request we remove you as a tester.
privacy.app_title: 4. The app: your devices and your iCloud
privacy.app_p: Not Yet works without an account. Everything you create or change in the app, such as routines, runs, to-dos and their planned times, alarms, bedtime plans, water, coins, rewards, NFC tag links, lock settings and the websites you add to the filter, is stored on your iPhone. The app shares it only with its own widgets, Live Activities and system extensions, your paired Apple Watch and, if you turn on “Add to Calendar”, its own calendar in Apple Calendar (section 6) and, if you turn on the iCloud backup, the private database of your own iCloud (see below).
privacy.app_p2: The app has no server and sends none of this data to us. Apart from the iCloud backup, if you turn it on, it sends it to no one else either. It contains no analytics, advertising or tracking tools and no third-party code that sends data. It works fully offline; only the iCloud backup needs a connection.
privacy.app_p3: If you back up your iPhone to iCloud or to a computer, iOS also includes the app’s data in that backup, under Apple’s terms and in your own account. That is one way your routines move to a new iPhone; Not Yet’s own iCloud backup is the other. We have no access to your iCloud. Deleting the app deletes its data from your iPhone, but not your backups.
privacy.backup_p1: Not Yet can keep a backup of your data in your own iCloud. It is off by default: only you can turn it on, in the app’s Settings under “iCloud backup” or during setup, and you can turn it off there at any time. While it is on, the app backs up when you leave it, at most once an hour and only if something has changed. When you set up Not Yet on a new or reset iPhone, the app looks for a backup in your iCloud and offers to restore it. Whether it does is up to you.
privacy.backup_p2: A backup contains the app’s database, with your routines, to-dos, runs, coins, rewards and kiosk, NFC tag links and settings, plus your alarm, bedtime and lock plans. To tell backups apart, each one also stores the device model, the app version, how many routines, to-dos and coins you have and the number of your last run. Permissions such as Screen Time, alarms, notifications or Apple Health are not part of a backup; you grant them again after a restore.
privacy.backup_p3: The backup is stored with Apple’s CloudKit in the private database of your own iCloud account (container iCloud.com.decudo.notyet) and counts against your iCloud storage. Apple stores it encrypted: the copy of the database as an encrypted file, the settings and the details above as encrypted fields. Only the time of each backup and a random ID of the installation stay unencrypted, so the app can sort and tidy up your backups. If you turn on Advanced Data Protection for iCloud, this encryption is end-to-end and only your trusted devices hold the keys; without it, Apple holds them, as for most iCloud data.
privacy.backup_p4: We have no access to your private iCloud database, and no server of ours is involved: the backup goes directly from your iPhone to Apple. Apple provides iCloud as its own service under the iCloud terms and Apple’s privacy policy. Where data protection law treats the backup as processing on our part, the legal basis is the app function you chose to use (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).
privacy.backup_p5: The app keeps the last 3 backups of each installation and deletes older ones. It also deletes the backups of an installation that hasn’t made a new one for 180 days. Turning the backup off or deleting the app keeps your existing backups. You can see them in the app under Settings > iCloud backup > Backups. To delete them, open the Settings app on your iPhone and go to [your name] > iCloud > Storage (or Manage Account Storage) > Not Yet.
privacy.watch_p: The Not Yet app on Apple Watch gets your plan for the day directly from your iPhone through Apple’s WatchConnectivity, and sends your taps back the same way. No server is involved, and nothing reaches us.
privacy.permissions_p: Each permission is optional. The app asks only when you use the feature, and you can change your choice at any time in the iOS Settings app.
privacy.permissions_p2: Reminders for routines, planned to-dos, sidequests and water are scheduled locally on your iPhone. They are not sent through a server. The reminder for a planned to-do shows the to-do’s icon, drawn by the app on your iPhone. Live Activities on your Lock Screen are updated on the device.
privacy.permissions_p3: Alarms use Apple’s AlarmKit so they ring even in silent mode. They are scheduled on your iPhone.
privacy.permissions_p4: If an alarm task asks you to walk a few steps or shake your iPhone, the app reads the step count and motion sensors on the device, only while that task is open. Nothing is stored or sent.
privacy.permissions_p9: Not Yet uses Apple Health only if you turn it on, and asks for permission only then. With Walking, the app reads today’s step count to give you coins for it. With “Sync with Apple Health” under Water, the app writes every glass you log to Health as water and reads today’s water from Health, so glasses from other apps count too. Not Yet reads or writes no other health data. This data stays on your iPhone and in Health, is never sent to us and is never used for advertising. You can withdraw the permission at any time in the Health app.
privacy.permissions_p5: If you allow calendar access, Not Yet reads only the calendars you pick in the app: for birthday to-dos, for ending a sidequest before your next appointment and for showing your appointments in Week. It reads them on your iPhone, never changes them and doesn’t copy them anywhere.
privacy.permissions_p5b: Not Yet writes to Apple Calendar only if you turn on “Add to Calendar” (part of Not Yet Plus). It then creates its own calendar called “Not Yet” and adds your planned to-dos to it: title, time, a short note and a link back to the app, without alerts. Changing a to-do updates its entry; finishing or deleting it removes the entry. Turning the switch off deletes the calendar. If you use iCloud for your calendars, Apple syncs this calendar through iCloud to your devices, like your other calendars; otherwise it stays on your iPhone. Not Yet itself sends nothing anywhere, and nothing reaches us.
privacy.permissions_h35: Screen Time: Focus lock, Bedtime lock and Adult sites
privacy.permissions_p6: The locks and the filter for adult websites use Apple’s Screen Time interface (Family Controls). The apps you choose are stored by iOS as opaque tokens on your iPhone. Not Yet can’t see which apps they are, and no usage data leaves your device. The filter for adult websites is Apple’s own filter, applied by iOS on your iPhone; the websites you add yourself are stored only there.
privacy.permissions_p7: An NFC tag written by Not Yet contains only a link with a random ID, like https://not-yet.app/t/7xk2ab9pqd. Which routine a tag starts is stored only in the app on your iPhone. If a phone without the app scans the tag, it opens that page on this website; the ID says nothing about you, and the visit counter doesn’t record it.
privacy.permissions_p8: So that such links can open the app, iOS checks a small file from this website through Apple’s servers (Associated Domains). That exchange happens between your iPhone and Apple.
privacy.sharing_p: Run cards are images the app creates on your iPhone. They are only shared when you share them yourself through the iOS share sheet, with the app or person you choose. The same goes for the alarm log, a hidden diagnostic list you can share as text if we ask for it to fix an alarm problem.
privacy.purchases_p: You buy Not Yet Plus in the App Store. Apple handles the purchase, the payment and any subscription renewals. We receive no payment data, no name and no Apple ID. Offer codes and gift codes are redeemed through Apple too.
privacy.purchases_p2: To know whether Plus is active, the app checks the purchase information that Apple provides through StoreKit on your iPhone. That check happens on the device. The app sends nothing about it to us, and there is no server of ours that could store it. In App Store Connect, Apple shows us only sales figures that don’t identify you.
privacy.purchases_p3: You manage or cancel a subscription in your Apple Account settings. If you share Plus through Family Sharing, Apple handles that as well. For the payment itself, Apple’s privacy policy applies.
privacy.testflight_p: You install Not Yet from Apple’s App Store. If you have turned on “Share With App Developers” in the iOS analytics settings, Apple gives us crash reports and usage figures in App Store Connect. These don’t identify you.
privacy.rights_p: You have the right of access (Art. 15 GDPR), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 17), restriction of processing (Art. 18) and data portability (Art. 20), and the right to object to processing based on legitimate interests (Art. 21). To exercise them, email info@not-yet.app. Since the app keeps your data only on your devices and in your own iCloud, the only personal data we hold are the emails you send us and, if you test the beta, your tester entry in App Store Connect. The visit counts on this website can’t be linked to you.
privacy.rights_p2: You can also complain to a data protection supervisory authority.
privacy.rights_p3: We update this policy when the app or the website changes. The date at the top shows the current version.
privacy.h1: Your routines stay on your iPhone.
privacy.short_dd_visits: This website counts visits on our own Umami server, without cookies and without storing IP addresses. You can opt out.
privacy.visits_p1: We count visits to this website with Umami, an open-source analytics tool, on an instance we run ourselves at a.not-yet.app. The server is hosted by Hetzner Online GmbH, Industriestraße 25, 91710 Gunzenhausen, Germany, in a data centre in Nuremberg. No analytics company or ad network is involved, and the data is not passed on, not sold and not combined with other data.
privacy.visits_p2: For each visit, Umami records the page, the referring page, the browser, the operating system, the device type and the country, which it derives from your IP address. The IP address itself is not stored. We also count clicks on the App Store and TestFlight links, the language menu and the dark mode switch. On NFC tag pages only /t/ is counted, never the tag ID.
privacy.visits_p3: Umami sets no cookies, builds no profiles and doesn’t follow you to other websites. We only see totals, which can’t be traced back to you.
privacy.visits_p4: Legal basis is our legitimate interest in knowing how the website is used, so we can improve it (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
privacy.visits_optout: Don’t want to be counted? Turn the switch below off. Your browser then stores umami.disabled in its local storage, and the counting script isn’t even loaded. A content blocker has the same effect; nothing on this website depends on it.
privacy.optout_label: Count my visits on this website
privacy.visits_app: The app itself has no analytics and sends nothing to us. The visit counter is for this website only and has no connection to the app.
privacy.testflight_p2: If you test new versions through Apple’s TestFlight and send feedback or screenshots there, or if a test version crashes and you have agreed to share the crash report, Apple passes this on to us in App Store Connect, together with technical data such as device model, iOS version and app version. We use it only to fix problems. Legal basis is our legitimate interest in a working app (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). Apple’s own processing is covered by Apple’s privacy policy.

support.title: Support
support.description: Help with Not Yet: getting the app, alarms, locks, the Lock Screen, Apple Watch, NFC tags and your data.
support.lead: Write to info@not-yet.app. A real person reads every message. It helps to mention your iPhone model, your iOS version and the app version.
support.alarm_a: Open the iOS Settings app, go to Not Yet and check that Alarms are allowed. Then open the alarm in Not Yet and make sure its switch is on and the right days are picked.
support.lock_q: Focus lock or Bedtime lock doesn’t block anything.
support.lock_a: The locks need your permission. In Not Yet, open the lock and pick the apps again; iOS asks for access the first time. For Bedtime lock, also check under Nights that tonight’s plan has “Lock apps” turned on. If Screen Time is turned off in Settings, the locks can’t work.
support.lockscreen_q: My routine doesn’t show up on the Lock Screen.
support.lockscreen_a: Check that notifications and Live Activities are allowed for Not Yet in the iOS Settings app, and that the routine has a time set.
support.watch_q: The watch shows an old plan.
support.watch_a: Open Not Yet on your iPhone once. The watch gets its plan from the iPhone and catches up as soon as both are connected.
support.calendar_q: Planned to-dos don’t show up in my calendar.
support.calendar_a: In Not Yet, open Settings › Calendar and turn on “Add to Calendar”. iOS asks for calendar access the first time. The to-dos then appear in a calendar called “Not Yet”; check that it’s ticked in the Calendar app.
support.nfc_q: My NFC tag opens a web page instead of the app.
support.nfc_a: That page appears when Not Yet isn’t installed, or when iOS hasn’t linked not-yet.app to the app yet. Tap “Open Not Yet” on the page. If it keeps happening, delete and reinstall the app, then scan the tag again.
support.data_q: How do I delete my data?
support.data_a: Everything lives on your iPhone, on your watch, in your iPhone backups and, if you turned it on, in Not Yet’s own backup in your iCloud. Deleting the app deletes its data, but not your backups. To delete Not Yet’s backup, open Settings on your iPhone and go to [your name] > iCloud > Storage (or Manage Account Storage) > Not Yet. We don’t keep a copy. If you emailed us, we delete those messages on request.
support.more: More answers are in the FAQ. How we handle data: privacy policy.
support.app_q: Where do I get Not Yet?
support.app_a: Download Not Yet on the App Store. It needs iOS 26 or later. To try new versions early, join the beta on TestFlight.

alarm.title: Alarm Clock With Tasks and No Snooze · Not Yet
alarm.description: An iPhone alarm clock that rings even on silent and has no snooze. It goes quiet only after a short task: three sums, 30 steps, a shake or an NFC tag.
alarm.lead: Most alarms stop with one tap, and you can manage that without waking up. This one goes quiet only after a short wake-up task, so by the time it’s off, you’re up.
alarm.alt_hero: The alarm ringing at 6:15: “Good morning.” and the “Wake-up task” button.
alarm.problem_p1: Half asleep, you can find the snooze button with your eyes closed. Five more minutes turns into an hour, and you never really decided anything. After a few weeks of the same tone, it gets easy to sleep right through it, too.
alarm.problem_p2: Not Yet takes the snooze out and puts one small task in. Nothing hard. Just enough that your head has to switch on before the alarm switches off.
alarm.s1_lead: Set as many alarms as you like, with days and a name, like in the Clock app.
alarm.s1_1_p: Through silent mode and any Focus, with a different tone each time, so your ears don’t tune it out.
alarm.s1_2_p: Slide to stop or press a button, and it rings again a few seconds later. There’s no snooze.
alarm.s1_3_p: Tap “Wake-up task” and Not Yet opens a short task. Get one wrong and you simply get a new one. No red, no counting.
alarm.s1_4_p: The alarm is off. If you picked a routine for after the alarm, it starts right away, and you can check off its steps on the Lock Screen.
alarm.alt_s1: Lock Screen after the alarm: the morning run has started, with the current step and a Done button.
alarm.s2_lead: Choose which kinds can come up. Each time, one is picked at random, never the same one twice in a row, and you only find out which when it rings.
alarm.s2_3_p: Three quick ones: a tear, a stamp, a tap.
alarm.s2_5_p: Walk 30 steps. To the kitchen and back works.
alarm.s2_6_p: Your NFC tag, say by the bathroom sink. You have to get up for that one.
alarm.s2_7_p: The first step of your routine after the alarm.
alarm.note_p: If your apps lock at night, a finished wake-up task can unlock them, so the night ends when you’re actually up. More about the app locks
alarm.faq1_q: Does the alarm ring when my iPhone is on silent?
alarm.faq1_a: Yes. It rings through silent mode and through any Focus. The volume follows Ringtone & Alerts in your iPhone’s settings, so make sure that isn’t turned all the way down.
alarm.faq2_a: No. Stopping it only ends that ring. It rings again a few seconds later, until the wake-up task is done. If nobody does it, it gives up after an hour.
alarm.faq3_q: What tasks can the alarm ask for?
alarm.faq3_a: Three sums, tapping 1 to 5 in order, a few quick moves with your fingers, shaking your phone, walking 30 steps, scanning an NFC tag or the first step of your morning routine. You pick which ones can come up.
alarm.faq4_q: Can it start my morning routine?
alarm.faq4_a: Yes. Pick a routine for after the alarm. Once the task is done, it starts as a run with the first step ready, and you can check off steps right on the Lock Screen.
alarm.faq5_q: Is it a good alarm clock for ADHD?
alarm.faq5_a: It was built with ADHD in mind: no snooze to bargain with, and tasks short enough for a foggy head. It works the same for anyone who sleeps through alarms.

applock.title: App Blocker for Focus and Bedtime · Not Yet
applock.description: Lock the apps that pull you away, for an hour of focus or for the whole night, until you’re up. Not Yet never sees which apps you pick.
applock.lead: Focus lock blocks distracting apps while you work. Bedtime lock keeps them locked at night, until you’re up. You decide once, ahead of time.
applock.alt_hero: Home in the morning: Focus lock is on, 42 minutes left.
applock.problem_p1: You pick up your phone to check the time, and forty minutes later you’re still scrolling. At night it’s one more video, then another. Saying no every single time is the hard part.
applock.problem_p2: An app blocker says it for you. You decide once, in advance. When the moment comes, the app doesn’t open, and there’s nothing to negotiate.
applock.s1_title: Focus lock: for the next hour.
applock.s1_lead: For work, studying or anything else that needs your attention for a while.
applock.s1_1_t: Allow a few, or block a few.
applock.s1_1_p: Keep only what you need, like Messages, Maps and Music, or lock just the apps that pull you away: social, games, video. Websites you pick count the same way.
applock.s1_2_p: Tap the lock on Home and pick how long, from 15 minutes to 4 hours. Or press and hold the app icon for 25 or 50 minutes.
applock.s1_3_p: Turn it on for runs and sidequests. It locks while your routine is on and ends when you’re done.
applock.s2_lead: Plan your nights like alarms: one for weekdays, one for the weekend. 23:00 to 7:00 to start with, and a quiet heads-up half an hour before.
applock.s2_1_p: Before bedtime, Home says nothing needs doing and water nudges stop. Then the apps you picked lock, from your focus list or a list just for the night.
applock.s2_2_p: Your apps unlock at your wake-up time, or as soon as you’ve done your alarm’s wake-up task.
applock.s2_3_p: Make an NFC tag your key and stick it somewhere you have to get up for, like the bathroom mirror. Then only that tag ends the night.
applock.s2_4_p: It locks the apps you pick, not the whole phone. Leave Clock unlocked so you can set your alarm.
applock.alt_s2: Nights: plans for office days, work-from-home days and the weekend, with wind-down before bedtime.
applock.note_title: Not Yet never sees your apps.
applock.note_p: You pick them in Apple’s own picker, and iOS keeps your choice on your iPhone in a form Not Yet can’t read. No usage data leaves your phone. No account, no tracking in the app.
applock.faq1_q: Can it block apps at night?
applock.faq1_a: Yes. Bedtime lock locks the apps you pick on the nights you planned, until your wake-up time or until your alarm’s task is done. With an NFC tag as your key, only that tag ends the night.
applock.faq2_a: Any apps and app categories you pick, plus websites. Either lock just those, or lock everything except the few you allow.
applock.faq3_q: Can Not Yet see which apps I use?
applock.faq3_a: No. The picker belongs to iOS, and Not Yet only gets a list it can’t read. Nothing about your app use leaves your iPhone.
applock.faq4_q: Do I need a routine to use the locks?
applock.faq4_a: No. Focus lock and Bedtime lock work on their own. If you do use routines, Focus lock can switch on with every run.
applock.faq5_q: Is it an app blocker for ADHD?
applock.faq5_a: It was built with ADHD in mind: the decision happens once, ahead of time, instead of every time you reach for your phone. It helps anyone who loses evenings to the feed.

routines.title: ADHD Routine App That Changes Before It Gets Old · Not Yet
routines.description: Morning routines that change how they play every few runs: wheel, dice, boss fight. Check off steps on the Lock Screen or Apple Watch. No streaks.
routines.h1_2: that changes before it gets old.
routines.lead: Your steps stay the same. The way the routine plays changes every few runs, and you can start it and check off steps without opening the app.
routines.alt_hero: Morning run with a boss fight: the longest step is the boss and comes last.
routines.problem_title: Routine apps get boring. Then they get deleted.
routines.problem_p1: A new routine app feels good for a week or two. Same list, same checkbox, every morning. Then the novelty wears off, a streak breaks, and the app ends up in a folder you never open.
routines.problem_p2: Not Yet keeps your steps and changes the game around them, before your head gets bored.
routines.s1_lead: Set up your routine once, step by step. Every few runs, the way it plays changes, and never back to one of the last two.
routines.s1_1_t: How the next step is picked
routines.s1_1_p: Wheel, Dice, Cards, Countdown, Blind run or Boss fight, where the longest step is the boss and comes last.
routines.s1_2_p: Stamp the card, tear the Ticket, click the Tally counter, hold until the Rocket lifts off, and more.
routines.s1_3_p: Only half the steps today, a bonus step, or a line to yourself that turns up on the next run.
routines.s2_lead: When it’s time, the routine comes to you.
routines.s2_1_p: At its time, your routine shows up with a Start button. Then the current step, with Done right next to it.
routines.s2_2_p: The next routine or the current step on your Home Screen, checked off with a tap.
routines.s2_3_p: Start a run, check off steps and log water from your wrist.
routines.s2_4_p: Tap the tag on your bathroom mirror, and the routine that belongs there starts.
routines.s2_5_p: Pick a routine for after your alarm. It starts as soon as the wake-up task is done.
routines.alt_s2: Lock Screen with the morning run: check off the current step right there.
routines.s3_lead: Every time you do a routine is a run with its own number. All of it, some of it or stopped early: it counts.
routines.s3_1_p: Steps, to-dos, sidequests and glasses of water earn coins. One step per run is golden and earns more.
routines.s3_2_p: At the end of a run, the coins sit in a piggy bank. A few hits, and it breaks.
routines.s3_3_p: Spend coins on what you pick, like a coffee or an episode, or on hammers and piggy skins in the Kiosk.
routines.s3_4_t: Sidequests for the time in between
routines.s3_4_p: Got 30 minutes? Say how much time you have and get one to-do that fits.
routines.s3_5_t: A short one after a break
routines.s3_5_p: Back after a few days? Your first run is shorter. Nothing mentions the pause.
routines.alt_s3: Run end: Run #24, some of it, a piggy bank to smash.
routines.faq1_q: How is it different from a habit tracker?
routines.faq1_a: There are no streaks, no percentages and no calendar of gaps. Each run has a number, and whatever you finish counts. What changes is the game, not the score.
routines.faq2_q: Can I check off steps without opening the app?
routines.faq2_a: Yes. At its time, the routine shows up on your Lock Screen. Start it and check off each step there, in a widget or on your Apple Watch.
routines.faq3_q: Which ways to play are there?
routines.faq3_a: Wheel, Dice, Cards, Countdown, Blind run and Boss fight pick the next step. Seven gestures check it off, from a stamp to a rocket. Twists like Only half come on top.
routines.faq4_q: What happens if I skip a few days?
routines.faq4_a: Nothing counts down and nothing turns red. When you come back after a longer break, your first run is a short one.
routines.faq5_q: Is Not Yet a routine app for ADHD?
routines.faq5_a: Yes. It was built with ADHD in mind: short steps, a routine that changes before it gets boring, and no streaks to lose. No diagnosis needed.

nights.title: Bedtime Routine App With Wind-Down and App Lock · Not Yet
nights.description: Plan your nights like alarms: a bedtime for each kind of day, a wind-down before it, and apps that stay locked until you’re up.
nights.lead: Plan your nights like alarms, one plan for each kind of day. First you wind down, then the apps you picked stay locked until you’re up.
nights.alt_hero: Nights: plans for office days, work-from-home days and the weekend, with wind-down before bedtime.
nights.problem_title: The day doesn’t end. It fades into the feed.
nights.problem_p1: Bedtime is a number you set once and then scroll right past. One more video, one more thread, and it’s one in the morning. Then the alarm rings, and the next day starts tired.
nights.problem_p2: Nights gives the evening a shape: a time when things wind down, a time when the apps go quiet and a time when you’re up. You set it once. After that, the evening runs on its own.
nights.s1_lead: Every morning belongs to one plan. It starts with one plan, 23:00 to 7:00, and you add your own.
nights.s1_1_t: One plan per kind of day
nights.s1_1_p: Office days, work-from-home days, the weekend. Each plan has its own bedtime and wake-up time.
nights.s1_2_p: Choose which nights lock your apps. The weekend can stay open.
nights.s1_3_p: Half an hour before the lock, a note without a sound.
nights.s2_title: Wind down first. Then lights out.
nights.s2_lead: Wind down starts 30 minutes to 3 hours before bedtime, or right after your evening routine.
nights.s2_1_p: Home says nothing needs doing. A planned to-do you didn’t get to leaves the day and stays on your list.
nights.s2_2_p: Water reminders come only between getting up and winding down. Nothing pings you in bed.
nights.s2_3_t: An evening routine, if you like
nights.s2_3_p: Phone on the charger, tomorrow’s clothes, teeth, lights out. Wind down can start once it’s done.
nights.s2_4_p: At bedtime, the apps you picked lock, from your focus list or a list just for the night.
nights.s2_5_p: Your apps unlock at your wake-up time, or as soon as you’ve done your alarm’s wake-up task.
nights.alt_s2: The alarm ringing at 6:15, with the “Wake-up task” button.
nights.s2_note: More about the app locks and the alarm clock.
nights.note_p: Week shows when you’re up on each of the next seven days, and planned to-dos leave the day once wind down starts. More about Week
nights.faq1_q: Can I set different bedtimes for weekdays and weekends?
nights.faq1_a: Yes. Make a plan for each kind of day, like office days, home days and the weekend. Every morning belongs to exactly one plan, with its own bedtime and wake-up time.
nights.faq2_a: Home says nothing needs doing, water nudges stop, and a planned to-do you didn’t get to leaves the day but stays on your list. Wind down starts 30 minutes to 3 hours before bedtime, or after your evening routine.
nights.faq3_q: Does it lock my whole phone at night?
nights.faq3_a: No. It locks the apps you pick, on the nights you choose. They unlock at your wake-up time or once your alarm’s wake-up task is done.
nights.faq4_q: Do I have to use the lock?
nights.faq4_a: No. Wind down and the pause in water nudges work without it. Turn the lock on for the plans where you want it.
nights.faq5_q: Is it a bedtime app for ADHD?
nights.faq5_a: It was built with ADHD in mind: you decide about the evening once, ahead of time, not at midnight with your phone in your hand. It works the same for anyone who loses nights to the feed.

week.title: Weekly Planner App for To-dos and Routines · Not Yet
week.description: See the next seven days with routines, alarms, birthdays and events. Drop a to-do into a free spot: roughly then, not a deadline. Nothing turns red.
week.lead: Tap the date on Home to see the next seven days. Drop a to-do into a free spot: roughly then, not a deadline. Nothing turns red when it slips.
week.alt_hero: Week: a birthday, the morning routine, an alarm and a free spot with the to-dos that fit it.
week.problem_p1: A to-do with a due date is a small promise. Miss it, and it sits there in red, listing what you didn’t do. After a few of those, opening the planner feels worse than not planning at all.
week.problem_p2: Week works the other way round. You don’t set a deadline, you find a gap: Tuesday, 15:00, about 30 minutes. If it happens, nice. If not, the to-do goes back to your list without a fuss.
week.s1_title: The next seven days, at a glance.
week.s1_lead: Week starts today and shows what’s already there, so you can see where the gaps are.
week.s1_1_p: Your morning routine, the evening one, the alarm that wakes you. Each at its time.
week.s1_2_p: Appointments from the calendars you pick, and birthdays that turn into a step in that day’s routine.
week.s1_3_p: Under each day, a small dot for a birthday, an appointment or a planned to-do. Ordinary days stay plain.
week.s1_4_p: No empty grid, no percentages. A day with nothing on shows its date and when you’re up.
week.alt_s1: Home in the morning: tap the date at the top to open Week.
week.s2_title: Plan a to-do into a free spot.
week.s2_lead: Tap “Plan”, pick a to-do, then tap a free time. Or tap the space between two things and see what fits there.
week.s2_1_p: A planned to-do has a time, not a deadline. When it’s time, the reminder shows the to-do’s icon.
week.s2_2_p: Each free spot shows the to-dos short enough for it.
week.s2_3_p: Hold a planned to-do to change its time, move it to another day or take it off the week. It stays on your list.
week.s2_4_p: If it doesn’t happen, it fades at its time and leaves the day in the evening. No overdue list, no counting.
week.s2_5_p: If you like, planned to-dos also show up in your calendar app, in a calendar of their own.
week.note_p: That’s a sidequest: say how much time you have, and Not Yet picks one to-do that fits. More about routines and sidequests
week.faq1_a: No, it sits next to your calendar. Week shows your routines, alarms and planned to-dos, along with events and birthdays from the calendars you pick. You plan to-dos here; appointments stay in your calendar app.
week.faq2_q: What if I don’t get to a planned to-do?
week.faq2_a: Nothing bad happens. It fades at its time and leaves the day in the evening. It stays on your to-do list, and nothing is marked overdue.
week.faq3_q: How far ahead can I plan?
week.faq3_a: Week shows today and the six days after it. That’s far enough to plan and short enough to take in at a glance.
week.faq4_q: Is it a weekly planner for ADHD?
week.faq4_a: It was built with ADHD in mind: no deadlines to miss, nothing red, and a plan you can move with one hold. It works for anyone who likes a loose plan better than a strict one.
